title.zh: 原子氢电荷交换Maxwellian速率系数

summary: H + H+ charge-exchange rate coefficient in m^3/s for paired plasma temperature and impact energy in eV. The legacy bivariate fit is retained through 20.1 keV; above that range the rate is integrated from the continuous Janev/Lindsay-Stebbings cross section against an equal-mass Maxwellian target.

capability: Paired Maxwellian temperature and impact energy -> H + H+ charge-exchange rate coefficient in m^3/s.
operation: Evaluate the atomic-H charge-exchange rate coefficient
paired plasma temperature and impact energy in eV -> rate coefficient in m^3/s
discovery.model: Nine-by-nine bivariate logarithmic fit through 20.1 keV, with a Maxwellian relative-speed quadrature of the continuous composite cross section above that domain.
discovery.geometry: None; paired scalar or array material samples with no spatial or velocity axis inferred (coordinates: temperature and impact energy in eV).
discovery.boundary: Finite real inputs with identical shape; temperature strictly positive and impact energy nonnegative. Low values clip to 0.1 eV; values above 250 keV clip with RuntimeWarning. The high-energy quadrature omits collision energies above 250 keV.

identity.relation: H + H+ charge-exchange rate coefficient from a low-domain bivariate fit or a high-energy Maxwellian integral
identity.direction: paired plasma temperature and impact energy in eV -> rate coefficient in m^3/s
identity.definition: For each paired sample, if T <= 2.01e4 eV and E <= 2.01e4 eV, clip both to [0.1, 2.01e4] eV and evaluate the legacy nine-by-nine logarithmic polynomial with the declared term order, returning exp(log_rate)*1e-6 m^3/s. Otherwise clip T and E to [0.1, 2.5e5] eV and integrate the continuous composite cross section against the equal-mass Maxwellian relative-speed density; collision energies above 2.5e5 eV are omitted. Values above 2.5e5 eV emit RuntimeWarning.
identity.model: piecewise low-domain bivariate fit and high-energy Maxwellian quadrature of the published composite cross section
identity.geometry: none; paired scalar or array material samples
identity.coordinates: temperature and impact energy in eV; output rate coefficient in m^3/s
identity.boundary: finite real same-shape inputs; positive temperature; nonnegative energy; low-domain clipping to 0.1 eV and upper clipping at 250 keV with RuntimeWarning; finite positive result
assumptions: The legacy 9x9 coefficient table and accumulation order define the fit used through 2.01e4 eV.
Above 2.01e4 eV the rate is defined by the equal-mass Maxwellian integral of the separately exposed composite cross section, not by extending the bivariate fit.
The cross-section integral uses the declared particle mass rather than reduced mass, matching the repository Maxwellian convention.
The cross-section table ends at 250 keV; the quadrature sets larger collision energies to zero and does not claim a cross-section extrapolation.

inputs.name: temperature_ev
inputs.description: Plasma temperature for the low-domain fit or the high-energy Maxwellian integral.
inputs.shape: scalar or array; exactly the shape of energy_ev
inputs.constraints: Finite and strictly positive real values. Values below 0.1 eV clip; values above 2.5e5 eV clip with RuntimeWarning.

inputs.name: energy_ev
inputs.description: Impact energy paired with each temperature sample.
inputs.shape: scalar or array; exactly the shape of temperature_ev
inputs.constraints: Finite nonnegative real values with the same shape as temperature. Values below 0.1 eV clip; values above 2.5e5 eV clip with RuntimeWarning.

outputs.name: rate_m3_s
outputs.description: H + H+ charge-exchange rate coefficient from the piecewise fit/quadrature relation.
outputs.constraints: Finite and strictly positive on accepted inputs; the high-energy quadrature is a bounded model, not an unbounded extrapolation.

preconditions: The caller accepts the declared switch at 2.01e4 eV and supplies physically paired temperature and impact energy.
The caller accepts the high-energy quadrature convention that collision energies above 250 keV are omitted.
supported: Scalar and equal-shape array evaluation through the low-domain fit.
High-energy rate evaluation from the composite cross-section Maxwellian integral.
excluded: Molecular-hydrogen charge exchange, transport sources and collision-frequency assembly.
Cross-section values above 250 keV or extrapolation of the bivariate rate fit beyond 20.1 keV.
A claim of exact experimental rate validation beyond the published cross-section reliability.

failure_semantics.invalid_input: Non-real, non-finite, unequal-shape, nonpositive-temperature or negative-energy inputs raise ValueError; boolean, complex and numeric-string coercions are rejected.
failure_semantics.runtime_failure: A non-finite or nonpositive result raises ValueError. Temperature or energy above 2.5e5 eV emits RuntimeWarning and uses the clipped upper edge.

example.description: Mix a low-domain reference sample with the T=50 keV, E=100 keV high-energy quadrature case and verify upper clipping.
example.code:
import warnings
import numpy as np
from scirel.collisions import evaluate_atomic_hydrogen_charge_exchange_rate

t = np.array([1.0, 5.0e4])
e = np.array([1.0, 1.0e5])
r = evaluate_atomic_hydrogen_charge_exchange_rate(t, e)
assert r.shape == (2,) and np.all(np.isfinite(r)) and np.all(r > 0.0)
np.testing.assert_allclose(r[1], 1.2004964216070182e-14, rtol=1e-10, atol=0.0)
with warnings.catch_warnings(record=True) as caught:
    warnings.simplefilter('always')
    clipped = evaluate_atomic_hydrogen_charge_exchange_rate(np.array([3.0e5, 2.5e5]), np.array([1.0, 1.0]))
assert len(caught) == 1 and issubclass(caught[0].category, RuntimeWarning)
edge = evaluate_atomic_hydrogen_charge_exchange_rate(np.array([2.5e5, 2.5e5]), np.array([1.0, 1.0]))
np.testing.assert_allclose(clipped, edge, rtol=1e-12, atol=0.0)
example.expected: The low sample follows the legacy fit, the high sample is about 1.2005e-14 m^3/s, and values above 250 keV clip to the endpoint under one RuntimeWarning.

scope: Legacy reference values and an independent polynomial evaluation verify the unchanged fit on samples at or below 20.1 keV.
At T=50 keV and E=100 keV the high-energy result is compared with independent 2D Gauss-Legendre Maxwellian quadrature using the composite cross section.
Two quadrature resolutions agree within 0.2% of the implementation, and the old clipped endpoint is at least four times larger.
Direct tests cover upper clipping, warning behavior, scalar and array shapes, invalid domain and non-real input rejection.
The high-energy relation is defined by quadrature of the separately exposed cross-section asset; it does not relabel an extrapolated bivariate fit.
verification.evidence_ceiling: The tests establish the low-domain discrete polynomial, the high-energy Maxwellian integral against an independent 2D quadrature, clipping and failure semantics. They do not establish an experimental rate measurement, an unbounded cross-section tail above 250 keV, or public distribution rights.
known_limitations: The low-domain bivariate fit remains nonmonotonic in impact energy at 1000 eV; this is a fit property, not a physical threshold.
The high-energy quadrature omits collision energies above 250 keV; this is a declared cross-section-range boundary, not an extrapolation.
Below 5 eV the composite cross section uses the Janev lower-domain fit; the Lindsay-Stebbings table does not validate that low-energy part.
The high-energy branch is a model of an equal-mass Maxwellian target and does not establish a broader distribution or transport closure.
No independent experimental rate measurement or public distribution licence is established.
